newsitem.title: USA: Eighth 'Star Trek' tops them all at box office.
newsitem.headline: Eighth 'Star Trek' tops them all at box office.

text.p: The eighth "Star Trek" movie opened a new frontier in the science fiction franchise by earning $30.45 million at the box office in its first weekend, according to studio estimates released on Sunday.

The three-day figures for the critically acclaimed "Star Trek: First Contact" were the highest in the 17-year history of movies based on the television series, said Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc.
The previous three-day "Trek" record was held by "Generations," which earned $23.12 million in its first three days in 1994, excluding Thursday night previews, and went on to make $75.7 million.
The highest grossing "Star Trek" movie was 1986's "The Voyage Home," which ended up with $109.7 million domestically.
Last week's number one, "Space Jam," slipped to second with $16.6 million. Also down a notch was the Mel Gibson thriller "Ransom," with $13.7 million.
Opening in fourth was the Arnold Schwarzenegger Christmas comedy "Jingle All The Way," with $12.2 million.
Despite being slayed by film critics, the movie is Schwarzenegger's best comedy opening. His previous best was "Kindergarten Cop," which opened in 1990 with $11.2 million.
"Star Trek: First Contact" is the first to feature no one from the late Gene Roddenberry's original 1966-69 "Star Trek" television series.

Heading the cast is Patrick Stewart as Captain Jean-Luc Picar,d who battles "Borg" villains who try to control the present -- i.e. the 24th Century -- by sabotaging the past. Jonathan Frakes, who plays Commander William Riker, directed.
"You don't have to know anything about 'Star Trek' to really enjoy this movie," producer Rick Berman said in an interview.
The action, humor and the "remarkable bad guys" were bringing more than just "Star Trek" fanatics -- or "trekkies" -- into movie theaters, he said.

According to a Variety poll of critics in New York, Los Angeles and Washington, 24 liked it, three did not and eight were mixed. The movie's per-screen average of $10,829 from 2,812 screens was the highest in the top 10.

"Space Jam," which stars Michael Jordan of the Chicago Bulls as the coach of a Looney Tunes basketball team in a match against alien invaders, has grossed $48.6 million in 10 days. In its second weekend, the movie fell by 40 percent and its screen average is a solid $6,264. The movie is released by Warner Bros., a unit of Time Warner Inc..
After three weekends, Walt Disney Co.'s "Ransom" has earned $86.2 million. It fell 39 percent from last weekend and is now averaging $4,949 per screen.
"Jingle All The Way" stars Schwarzenegger as a harried father who fights Christmas shopping crowds and evil Santas in a relentless search for the Turboman action toy his son wants for Christmas.

Critics generally hated the movie, which is released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp. According to Variety, two liked it, 19 did not and four were mixed. The movie opened on 2,433 screens and averaged $5,077.

Down two places to fifth was "The Mirror Has Two Faces," which Barbra Streisand stars in and directed. It earned $8.2 million in its second weekend, falling 33 percent. Its 10-day total is $24.3 million. The movie is released by Sony Corp.'s TriStar Pictures.
Opening in limited release, on seven screens, was the Australian drama "Shine," based on the true story of pianist prodigy David Helfgott.
The movie, which is released by Time Warner's Fine Line Features, earned $164,000 for a per-screen average of $23,429. According to Variety, 31 critics liked it, two did not and five were mixed.
